clue.text: Snout reported in prison public fully recognises

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word for a snout is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a snout is a nose
someone serving time is said to be inside
something made public is out in the open

explanation.surface: A police informer's tip-off about a jail, with someone inside who knows all about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snout' looks like slang for an informer, but here it is just the nose, said out loud. 'Reported' signals that sound swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand something thoroughly is an idiom for knowing every detail of it, so the phrase means fully recognises.

clue.text: Maybe footballers close to promotion skipped in underwear

indicators.note: something skipped is left out, so a letter is dropped from the underwear

parts.note: knickers are underwear

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here from promotion

explanation.surface: Footballers jumping a division but being caught in their underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks footballers as one example of people who kick.
explanation.definitionFit: Footballers kick the ball, so they are an example of those who kick.

clue.text: Virtual assistant: 60 secs engaged in speech test

indicators.note: engaged in means held within, so these pieces go inside the speech

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech
Alexa is Amazon's voice-controlled virtual assistant
sixty seconds is a minute, abbreviated MIN

explanation.surface: A voice assistant gets a one-minute slot in a speaking exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, such as a viva, is a type of test.

clue.text: Overturning alcoholic drink is mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturning turns the word upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: pils is pilsner lager

explanation.surface: Knocking over a drink is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A small error or lapse is a common synonym, as in a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Bonehead in IT withholds screens

indicators.note: screens means conceals, so the letters lie concealed within these words

explanation.surface: A dim worker in the IT department keeps the monitors to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screens' suggests computer monitors in an IT office; it is a verb meaning hides.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is a stupid person, and this informal insult means the same.

clue.text: Vile reason an earl regularly stripped

parts.note: to infer is to reason or deduce

indicators.note: taking away letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is stripped of rank for a disgraceful reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellish or fiendish things are thoroughly wicked, so the word stands for vile.

clue.text: Horse-rider requests trial, one totally unlimited

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its limits, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A jockey asks for a trial, every restriction lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in riding horses is called by this name, so it is a horse-rider.

clue.text: No-one can rule pub out, it's impossible to say

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nobody can forbid a pub, and nobody can tell what will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A word too awkward to pronounce cannot be spoken, which is what impossible to say means.

clue.text: Yield when discharged

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sent means dispatched or discharged

explanation.surface: Giving in at the moment one is released.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield in the sense of giving way or agreeing is to give one's consent, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Racing vehicle in church, a fun event

parts.note: a riot is a great laugh, something hugely entertaining

explanation.surface: A racing car is brought into a church for some lively entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient chariots were raced in arenas like the Circus Maximus, so a chariot is a racing vehicle.

clue.text: For all to see in message, father's blunder

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here the film rating within the message

parts.note: a fax is a message sent by facsimile machine
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for everyone
pa is an informal word for father, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Dad's embarrassing mistake is put in a message where everyone can read it.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema rating for films anyone may watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means a false step, and is used in English for a social blunder.

clue.text: Vessel heading off later

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken off here

parts.note: something later is newer

explanation.surface: A ship sets off on its course, but only at a later time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A large jug or pitcher for water is a vessel in the container sense.

clue.text: Scientific tool that's rewritten comic prose

indicators.note: writing something out afresh puts the letters of these words into a new order

explanation.surface: Some comic writing has been reworked into a scientific instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifying instrument for viewing tiny objects is a standard piece of laboratory equipment.

clue.text: Exhibitionist who's tailored hat

indicators.note: tailored means altered to fit, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a boater is a flat-crowned straw hat

explanation.surface: Someone who shows off in a made-to-measure hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who seeks attention by flamboyant display is an exhibitionist.

clue.text: Injure head in smacking roughly against article

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, taken from the word smacking

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
the definite article in English

explanation.surface: A blow to the head from someone hitting out wildly against a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm or wound is an old sense of this verb, surviving mainly in its negative form unscathed.

clue.text: Execute bishop, second person snared by queen, maybe

indicators.note: something snared is caught inside, so these pieces sit within the cat

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, one example of the animal
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
you is the second-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A chess scene: put to death a bishop, while another piece is captured by the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting misleads: the queen is a female cat, and 'Execute' means perform, not kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute a plan is to perform or accomplish it, the phrasal verb's everyday sense.

clue.text: City's chapter gathering both sides in part of church

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the sides are placed inside the church part

parts.note: an aisle is a passage in a church
both sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A cathedral chapter meets with people on both sides of the aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter' suggests a cathedral body; it is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: This Cumbrian city near the Scottish border has its own cathedral.

clue.text: Woolly garment's stain turned water hazy

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: turned means the word for a stain is read backwards

parts.note: ink leaves a stain

indicators.note: hazy suggests something blurred and muddled, so the letters of water are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wool jumper has been dyed by a cloudy dirty liquid in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing made by knitting, such as sweaters and cardigans, is a collective term for woolly garments.

clue.text: Kelvin casual, playing horn

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the temperature unit
lax means casual or slack
something playing is on, as a show is on

explanation.surface: A laid-back man called Kelvin blowing on a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric warning horn, once fitted to cars, is known by this trade name.

clue.text: Male in the morning penning antelope in oversize container

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the antelope is placed inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning
the gnu, or wildebeest, is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A man at dawn rounding up an antelope into an oversized enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bottle holding twice the usual amount is a large container of that name.

clue.text: Relatives married, not me

parts.note: others means everyone but me

explanation.surface: A grumble that the family has wed, but not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mum is a close relative, so the plural means relatives.

clue.text: Irritated chap cut short FBI agent

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter of chap goes

parts.note: a Fed is an American federal agent of the FBI

explanation.surface: A man is annoyed when a G-man interrupts him.
explanation.definitionFit: Being chafed is being rubbed raw, figuratively annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Clerics a Yankee has converted on coral island

indicators.note: on reads as next to or attached to, so the island joins up with the jumbled letters, landing within them

parts.note: Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: something converted is changed in form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: an atoll is a ring-shaped coral island

explanation.surface: An American has become a convert to a religious faith while living on a coral island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' looks like religious conversion, which suits clerics, but it is the signal to rearrange; 'on' sets the island alongside so it lands within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior Shia Muslim religious leaders in Iran bear this title, so they are clerics.

clue.text: Following cross, where ball would be for goal?

indicators.note: a scored ball sits inside the goal, so the cross is placed inside it

parts.note: the net is the goal in football
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A football cross into the box, and the question of where the ball will end up for a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a pass from the wing; it is just the X shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for whatever comes immediately after is a synonym of following.

clue.text: Rogue content in spiked headwear

indicators.note: rogue means wayward or wild, so the letters are jumbled
the content of a word is what lies inside its outer letters

explanation.surface: A villain's drink has been spiked, with a hat as the clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content in' takes PIKE from the inside of spiked; 'Rogue' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A French military cap with a flat top and visor is a kind of headwear.

clue.text: Drugs work, I answer group in review

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: looking back over something reverses it, so the word for group is read from the end

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A report on drug use: I am the response team assessing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics derived from opium, such as morphine, are drugs of this class.

clue.text: Fine ale around that is gift

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for ale is reversed

parts.note: ale is a beer
IE, from id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A good beer handed out at no charge is a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given away free of charge is an informal name for a gift.

clue.text: Hostility if elder nuns sin all over the place

indicators.note: scattered all over the place means these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Bad feeling arises in a convent when the elder sisters misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of friendliness amounts to hostility, coldness or antagonism toward others.
